reviewed_by: Claude (proxy-identity-encoding bug loop); selection reviewed against the diff by the implementing agent, root cause independently validated by a separate subagent
reason: RuntimeHttpProxy forwarded requests on a pooled httpx client that adds its own Accept-Encoding when the viewer sent none, so the project worker's GZipMiddleware compressed bodies of 1 KiB or more and the proxy forwarded the raw gzip bytes to clients that never negotiated it (curl, reqwest without gzip). The proxy now sends Accept-Encoding: identity upstream when the viewer sent none, and stops forwarding upstream date/server headers, which uvicorn repeated once per hop. Python: runtime_http (new regression: no-negotiation viewer gets plain JSON, gzip viewer still gets gzip, upstream server header dropped) and the API worker suite that wraps the same proxy.
exclusions: tests/v3/test_runtime_routing.py also passes locally (113 passed across the three files with PostgreSQL variants) but routing is unchanged, so it is not selected. Python's urllib sends Accept-Encoding: identity itself, so the deploy gate and deployer scripts were not affected. No UI, settings, catalog, product knowledge or native change. Revalidated on the staging Core: curl without Accept-Encoding gets plain JSON with one date and server header; curl --compressed, Chromium and WebKit still get gzip and decode it.
